method.host: WSL2 Linux; single host; standard asyncio
method.main_trials: 108 sequential randomized blocked trials: six temporal effects x four treatments x three repeats; E1.31 three traffic patterns x two paths x two treatments x three repeats.
method.dynamic_trials: 24 further sequential randomized paired trials: singleColor sine/breath, gradient roll, random_flash hit probability 0.5; threaded versus on-render cadence; three repeats, five-second measurement, two-second warmup.
method.randomization: Seed 2058 determines block and treatment order. Temporal Python/NumPy input seeds are 2058 + repeat. Sender inputs always use sender_bench.frame_pair seed 2058; the manifest seed field is unused for sender inputs.
method.provenance: Worker and prototype implementations frozen at bafe5673. Orchestrator resumed after 45 complete observations using ef9d591e/f327328f to handle null receive rates. Completed observations were retained; no worker/prototype timing code changed on resume. The single sparse-encode repeat-1 pair straddling the pause was rerun adjacently; its original observations are retained under paired/interrupted-pair and excluded from the final comparisons. Per-trial metadata records revision and working tree.

treatments.threaded-max: Uncapped render, preview and target effect producer. Scheduler yields retained. Fixture virtuals paced.
treatments.render-max: Uncapped render and preview; compute one effect update per rendered frame, ignoring normal effect speed/interval.
treatments.threaded-cadence: Uncapped render and preview; normal production temporal update pacing.
treatments.render-cadence: Uncapped render and preview; on-render update only when due, honoring speed/returned interval/minimum 1ms yield, coalescing late ticks. Render opportunities quantize updates and can reduce the update rate.

method.transport: Full 50k RGB websocket decoding and DDP to 127.0.0.2. Independent DDP receiver process. E1.31 encode discards socket writes; loopback receives and validates actual datagrams.
method.metrics: Delivery FPS is complete DDP frames. Changed-image FPS hashes/compares decoded websocket pixels. Effect FPS is effect_loop calls. Static windows count the first observed image as a change, giving about 1/window even for identical frames.
method.cpu_memory: 100% CPU is one server/sender core; client and receiver CPU excluded. RSS is an end-of-window snapshot including harness buffers, not peak memory or leak proof.
method.statistics: All three observations, medians, min/max and within-repeat paired ratios retained. No confidence interval or cross-machine generalization claimed from n=3.
method.sanity_checks: Cadence trials fail if effect FPS exceeds nominal*1.1 + 2/window. Exactly one output row required. Invalid packets and failed payload checks fail the trial. Gaps between complete and pushed frames are reported separately.

semantic_findings: Fade increments gradient position 0.0015 per update. Its nominal 5 Hz means 0.0075 gradient-position/s; advancing every high-rate render changes animation speed.

Rainbow increments hue 0.01 per update. Nominal benchmark 60 Hz means 0.6 hue/s. On-render cadence at a perfectly regular 500 Hz quantizes 60 Hz ticks to 18ms intervals: 112 updates in two seconds instead of 120. A deterministic real-effect test captures this.
SingleColor sine/breath modulation advances counters per update. Gradient roll advances per update too; static defaults hide these timing differences.
Pixels uses elapsed time but detects a modulo wrap, so long missed intervals can skip steps. Its configured speed 20 implies a nominal 200 Hz temporal worker.

RandomFlash hit probability is calibrated to 50 updates/s during inactive periods; the fade envelope uses elapsed time. Uncapping calls changes the probability distribution. The main fixture forces probability 1; the dynamic follow-up uses 0.5.
correctness_coverage: 21 layout/dtype combinations: 1/170/171/1000/50000 RGB pixels; 510/512 channels/universe; offsets 0/1/7/511/513; start universe 17; priority 177; uint8/float32/float64, including fractional truncation.

Full packet byte equivalence with only sequence counters masked; independent expected slot reconstruction; sentinel 93 retained outside driven slots; changed flag, destination/priority, instance isolation and restore checked.

Legacy setter equivalence at buffer lengths 0/1/127/510/511/512 and rejection of invalid lengths/channel values. Adapter is only for LedFx built-in integer lists after NumPy conversion, not a generic sACN API replacement.

All six real temporal classes activate, render finite 32x3 frames, shut down without producer threads and reactivate. Fake-clock tests cover speed/returned interval/minimum yield, late tick coalescing and phase behavior.
Experiment-design tests cover reproducible balanced blocks, within-repeat pairing, failed-trial exclusion, null encoding-only metrics and non-destructive resume.
limits: No physical LEDs, device firmware, LAN, Wi-Fi or Windows-native performance claim. No claim that the fake receiver represents a physical device capable of accepting these rates.

Only one websocket client; receiver/client CPU excluded. Live checks prove structural completeness, not cross-transport identity of concurrently rendered images. Sender microbench preflight checks exact expected payload bytes.

Per-call instrumentation appends timing samples. Uncapped overproducing temporal workers incur more instrumentation overhead and buffer allocation; saturation FPS is not an uninstrumented production guarantee.

Eight-second main and five-second dynamic windows are throughput comparisons, not thermal or memory-leak soak tests. Seeded random sources do not make wall-clock scheduling or stochastic animation histories identical.

Full 63-effect screening and targeted Python 3.15 CPU profiles from the preceding phase remain separate evidence. These repeated trials focus on the two experimental adapters, not every configuration of all effects.

The sACN prototype uses private per-instance class replacement solely in tools. Newly created/reconfigured outputs require reinstallation. A supported public byte-buffer setter upstream is needed before production adoption.
On-render cadence is not an elapsed-time animation model. Transitions, live configuration changes and every UI configuration are not validated for production adoption.

rejected_trials.reason: Aborted preliminary batch: threaded-cadence inherited an unpaced clock. Its effect rates were thousands per second instead of nominal. Excluded from all comparisons; explicit clock selection and a cadence sanity check prevent recurrence.

decisions.decision: Keep current scheduling. Across six main effects, cadence-controlled median complete-frame changes are within about 1%; Rainbow/Pixels/RandomFlash lose update cadence under on-render scheduling. Animated follow-ups show no consistent throughput advantage. The large uncapped gains are not a production-equivalent speedup.

Highest-confidence experimental candidate: about 2.4–2.5x encoding and 1.6x loopback throughput. Propose a supported immutable byte-buffer setter upstream before production adoption; do not ship the private class replacement.
Retain prior sampling priorities: Smoke 2D noise/draw and Melt & Sparkle triangle/sine work. Preserve visual/numeric behavior and compare repeated unprofiled trials.
